report.source_text: Clinical examination revealed bilateral conjunctival inflammation and three blister-type skin lesions on the arms and legs. Inspection of the oral cavity showed mucosal ulcerations of the ventral tongue (figure 1), cheeks, soft palate (figure 2), uvula and posterior oropharyngeal wall. A flexible transnasal endoscopy revealed crusts on the right middle turbinate and nasopharynx, as well as diffuse whitish pseudomembrane-covered erosions of almost all the supraglottic area and posterior hypopharyngeal wall (figure 3).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of diffuse oral burning sensation and disabling pharyngodynia, along with systemic symptoms and a history of breast and endometrial carcinoma. Clinical examination revealed bilateral conjunctival inflammation, blister-type skin lesions, and widespread mucosal ulcerations and erosions affecting the oral cavity, pharynx, larynx, and nasopharynx. A skin biopsy showed subepithelial cleavage, and direct immunofluorescence demonstrated linear IgG and C3 deposits at the dermo-epidermal junction. Immunoblotting identified circulating autoantibodies to BP180 and laminin 5. A PET-CT scan, performed due to the oncological history and anti-laminin 5 antibodies, revealed left supraclavicular and multiple retroperitoneal adenopathies. Based on these findings, a diagnosis of Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid (MMP) with diffuse involvement was made.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with diffuse oral burning sensation and disabling pharyngodynia.
Clinical examination revealed bilateral conjunctival inflammation, blister-type skin lesions, and widespread mucosal ulcerations/erosions in oral, pharyngeal, laryngeal, and nasal areas.
Skin biopsy showed subepithelial cleavage on routine histopathology.
Direct immunofluorescence revealed linear deposits of IgG and C3 at the dermo-epidermal junction.
Circulating autoantibodies to BP180 and laminin 5 were detected by immunoblotting.
PET-CT revealed left supraclavicular and multiple retroperitoneal adenopathies, relevant given the patient's history and anti-laminin 5 antibodies.
